record.summary: Decision of the Council of Ministers under Article 77(2) of the EU AI Act designating the Bulgarian authorities that supervise or enforce fundamental-rights law, including non-discrimination, in relation to high-risk AI systems. Seven bodies are designated: the Ombudsman, the Central Election Commission, the Commission for Protection against Discrimination, the Commission for Personal Data Protection, the Consumer Protection Commission, the State Agency for Child Protection and the General Labour Inspectorate. They may request and access documentation created under the AI Act where needed to exercise their powers.
record.notes: Published on the Council of Ministers' portal on 19 June 2025 (Protocol 25.28), submitted by the Ministry of e-Government. The decision does not designate market surveillance authorities, a notifying authority or a single point of contact and sets no penalties. According to Ministry of e-Government answers reported by BTA on 9 January 2026, a draft decision naming the Bulgarian Accreditation Service as notifying authority had not yet been submitted to the Council of Ministers, a draft decision on market surveillance had not entered interministerial coordination and the sanctions regime was undetermined. A private members' bill with a fuller framework was filed in September 2026 (BG-02).

verification.note: The decision's Word file (.doc) is stored but has no text layer, so its articles were not re-read this run. The Council of Ministers' portal page (strategy.bg) confirmed the number, issue date 18.06.2025, publication date 19.06.2025, legal basis, submitting ministry and the bodies named as terms; the Council's meeting agenda of 18 June 2025 confirmed adoption and the powers of access to documentation. The names of the seven bodies as a list and the 'no further designations' statements rest on the BTA report of the ministry's answers.
